title: Systematic CMB Constraints on Early-Universe Modifications: Parameter Degeneracies and Null Results
description: Implements two Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) mechanisms in CLASS—(i) a smooth modification to the photon–baryon coupling \dot{\kappa}(z) and (ii) a Gaussian-windowed, radiation-like background energy fraction \epsilon at recombination—and tests them against the Planck 2018 CMB TT spectrum with amplitude marginalization. A 2D parameter analysis shows both mechanisms yield null results once degeneracies with h are accounted for, turning an apparent 1D “detection” into a parameter-degeneracy artifact.

kappa_dot_mod.description: Smooth, localized modification to the photon–baryon coupling rate around z≈700; b is scanned in percent to test deviations from standard Thomson scattering.

rho_EFC_window.description: Gaussian-windowed, radiation-like energy fraction centered near recombination that perturbs H(z) by contributing a fraction \epsilon of the total energy density at that epoch.

chi2_amp_marg.description: Amplitude-marginalized chi-squared used to compare model spectra to Planck TT data while absorbing an overall calibration factor.

key_results.main_finding: Both tested EFC mechanisms are rejected by Planck 2018 TT once parameter covariances are accounted for; the apparent 1D signal for \epsilon vanishes in a 2D (\epsilon, h) analysis with the minimum at \epsilon≈0.

kill_criteria: KC1: A joint full-likelihood TTTEEE+lensing analysis (Planck18+ACT+SPT), marginalizing over standard ΛCDM parameters including h and τ, prefers a non-zero kappa-dot boost at z≈700 with |boost| ≥ 0.3% and Δχ² ≤ -9 (≈3σ) relative to ΛCDM, replicated across independent high-ℓ datasets—this would falsify the EFC-R expectation that the CMB epoch is an L0–L1 (standard-physics) regime.

KC2: The same joint analysis prefers a non-zero Gaussian-windowed, radiation-like component at recombination with |ε| ≥ 0.5% and Δχ² ≤ -9 after marginalizing h and other correlated parameters, and the result is stable under TT-only → TTTEEE and high-ℓ dataset swaps—this would falsify the EFC-R claim of no recombination-era modification.

KC3: A combined CMB (TTTEEE+lensing) + BAO + BBN + SNe fit requires a localized recombination-era excess radiation (w≈1/3) at ≥3σ to simultaneously match r_s and D_A, with consistent posteriors across likelihood choices—this would kill the EFC-R regime assignment that predicts standard physics during the CMB epoch.

KC4: Direct constraints on time-variation of the Thomson coupling from CMB anisotropies and damping-tail measurements detect a non-standard \dot{\kappa}(z) feature centered near z≈700 at ≥3σ independent of foreground modeling systematics—this would falsify the EFC-R assumption of standard microphysics in the CMB regime.
abstract_short: Both κ̇ and H(z) EFC mechanisms REJECTED against Planck 2018 CMB. 1D 'signal' was parameter degeneracy artifact. CMB epoch = L0-L1 regime where standard physics expected.
key_lesson: Parameter degeneracies can create false signals. Multi-dimensional analysis essential.

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper implements two recombination-era EFC mechanisms in CLASS and shows that, once h–epsilon covariances are properly accounted for with amplitude marginalization, Planck 2018 TT prefers no modification: both the kappa-dot boost and a Gaussian-windowed radiation-like epsilon at recombination collapse to null. It strengthens the EFC-R stance that the CMB epoch is an L0–L1 (standard-physics) regime and cautions against 1D scans that ignore parameter degeneracies.
graph_insights: No linked prior tests share these Planck TT observables in the graph, so adding explicit TT null-result tests will close a traceability gap.
The paper sits at the EFC-R validation node, linking early-universe mechanism prototypes (kappa-dot, epsilon) to Planck18 constraints and highlighting h–epsilon degeneracy edges.

tests_added.name: Planck18 TT: Smooth kappa-dot(z) tanh boost yields null preference after amplitude marginalization
tests_added.description: Evaluates whether a smooth ±(0.3–3)% tanh boost to the Thomson coupling around z≈700 improves the Planck18 TT fit beyond noise when amplitude-marginalized.
tests_added.prediction: EFC-R predicts no statistically significant preference for recombination-era microphysics modifications; best fit should be near zero boost with Δχ² consistent with noise.

tests_added.name: Planck18 TT: Gaussian-windowed radiation-like epsilon at recombination collapses after (epsilon,h) 2D analysis
tests_added.description: Checks that an apparent 1D TT preference for epsilon vanishes when jointly varying epsilon and h with amplitude marginalization, yielding a minimum near epsilon≈0 and Δχ² consistent with noise.
tests_added.prediction: EFC-R predicts no robust TT-only improvement from a localized radiation-like background at recombination once correlated parameters (notably h) are marginalized.

page_updates.new_text: A TT-only, amplitude-marginalized CLASS analysis of a Gaussian-windowed, radiation-like epsilon at recombination finds that the apparent 1D preference disappears in a joint (epsilon, h) treatment, with the minimum at epsilon≈0 and Δχ² consistent with noise (DOI:10.6084/m9.figshare.31095466). Full KC2 requires TTTEEE+lensing+high-ℓ; TT results are supportive but not decisive.
page_updates.reasoning: The paper directly tests the KC2 mechanism on TT and finds a null once degeneracies are accounted for; it informs but does not fulfill the KC2 joint-likelihood requirement.

page_updates.new_text: TT-only constraints on a smooth kappa-dot(z) boost centered at z≈700 yield a null result under amplitude marginalization (DOI:10.6084/m9.figshare.31095466). KC4 demands ≥3σ detections robust to foreground/high-ℓ choices; current TT evidence supports standard microphysics at recombination.
page_updates.reasoning: This specifically targets time-variation of the Thomson coupling and finds no evidence in TT; it contextually supports KC4 without completing the full multi-spectrum requirement.

implicit_consequences: Any prior 1D epsilon hints from TT are methodological artifacts of neglecting h covariance and should be retired from consideration.
Priority for full-likelihood TTTEEE+lensing and high-ℓ replication remains; EFCLASS development is still required to scale these tests beyond TT.
